clue.text: Condemnation of Davis; popular, strangely, but not one of us!

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the names and words before it are to be set out in an odd new order
but not tells us one letter is to be dropped from the word popular before mixing

parts.note: U is one of the two letters of the word us, and also the old label for the upper class who would call themselves 'one of us'

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that Davis, though popular, is oddly an outsider who earns disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes U from POPULAR, leaving POPLAR; 'strangely' then rearranges DAVIS plus POPLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Disapproval is a censure or expression of displeasure, the same as a condemnation.

clue.text: Rejecting anorak gets churchman very wet

indicators.note: rejecting sends the anorak's synonym back the other way

parts.note: in British slang an anorak is an obsessive, a nerd
CH is the abbreviation for church
Ed is a man's name, the man part of churchman

explanation.surface: A cleric who turns down a waterproof jacket gets soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang an anorak is an obsessive enthusiast, not only a coat; 'Rejecting' reads that word backwards. 'churchman' splits into church and a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Drenched means soaked through, wet to the skin.

clue.text: Understand supporter, about fifty, being less alert

indicators.note: about says the word for understand goes round the Roman numeral

parts.note: to see is to understand
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that a backer of about fifty is getting drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SEE around L to make SLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepier means drowsier, less wide awake.

clue.text: Tax oriental receiver

parts.note: PAYE, Pay As You Earn, is the British system of deducting income tax from wages
E for eastern, so oriental

explanation.surface: An Eastern tax is collected by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A payee is the person who is paid, the one getting the money.

clue.text: Self-restraint shown by substitute

definitions.meaning: reticence or holding back one's feelings
a player kept in readiness to replace another

explanation.surface: A replacement player shows notable composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticence is a holding back, and a sports team's replacement player waits on the bench.

clue.text: Woman has article to publish about pets' homes

parts.note: Viv is a woman's name, short for Vivien
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about says the word for publish is turned round

parts.note: to air a view is to publish or broadcast it

explanation.surface: A woman has an article out about animal housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivaria are enclosures for keeping live animals, such as reptile tanks.

clue.text: Glasses with which to watch trainee tenor get in a state

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

indicators.note: in a state means agitated, so the letters before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: A trainee tenor gets flustered about glasses for watching the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of opera spectacles held up on a handle.

clue.text: Sides' relationship with old island

definitions.meaning: in trigonometry the cosine, abbreviated ..., is the ratio between two sides of a right-angled triangle
The older spelling of the Greek island of Kos in the Aegean

explanation.surface: A remark on how two sides relate to an island of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: The trigonometric ratio of adjacent side to hypotenuse is written cos, and Cos is the classical name of a Dodecanese island.

clue.text: Middle course first, then most of main course

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word course
most of drops the final letter of the dish's name

parts.note: an entree is a main course, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: A menu note: start with one dish, then most of the main.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre is the middle point of something.

clue.text: Military investments

parts.note: investment in its old military sense is the surrounding of a town by an army, not putting money in

explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town is to surround and blockade it, so an army's investments are blockades of fortified places.

clue.text: Second in race trains to the utmost degree

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Second in race trains to the utmost degree': VERY can be 'to the utmost degree' but no parse of 'Second in race trains' gives the E; no scan and an exact-text search found nothing, so a word may be misread.
annotationWithheld.clue: Second in race trains to the utmost degree

clue.text: Cutting short clergyman's return in contact group

indicators.note: in tells us the turned clergyman goes inside the group's word

parts.note: a seance is a group gathered to make contact with the dead

indicators.note: return says the clergyman's short title is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone cuts short a vicar's comeback at a spiritualist meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads the clergyman's title backwards, and 'in' puts it inside the seance; 'short' simply goes with 'Cutting' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A severance is a cutting off, ending a link or tie abruptly.

clue.text: Triumphant skipper's servant

definitions.meaning: a winning captain lifts the trophy, so he literally carries the cup
in royal households an officer who poured and handed wine to the monarch

explanation.surface: A victorious team captain is described as somebody's attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning captain holds the trophy aloft, and historically a royal attendant poured wine for the king.

clue.text: Language used in Benin or Senegal

indicators.note: used in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundary

explanation.surface: A remark about which tongue is spoken in two West African countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'Benin or Senegal': beniN OR SEnegal.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the Scandinavian tongue of the Vikings.

clue.text: Eruption in orbit? Not a pretty sight!

definitions.meaning: read playfully, a spot or boil erupting in the eye socket
something ugly that spoils a view

explanation.surface: A painful spot in the eye is unpleasant to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orbit' suggests space and a volcanic eruption, but it is the eye socket.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsightly, such as an ugly building, spoils the view for everyone.

clue.text: One boss is struggling with dominant concern

indicators.note: struggling suggests things being thrown about, so the letters before it are mixed

explanation.surface: A manager is battling with a pressing worry.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a fixation that dominates the mind.

clue.text: Playbook?

parts.note: a book of the New Testament whose name is also the word for the main divisions of a stage drama

explanation.definitionFit: Plays are divided into these sections, and it is the name of a New Testament book, so a play-word that is a book.

clue.text: Vegan is first to mix wines

indicators.note: mix says the gathered letters are stirred into a new order
first takes the opening letter of the word to

explanation.surface: A vegan is the first to blend different wines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives T from 'to'; 'mix' rearranges VEGAN, IS and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintages are wines of a particular year's harvest.

clue.text: Small exercise areas set in soft prisons

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
to lay something is to set it down
a pen is an enclosure or, in American slang, a prison

explanation.surface: Little exercise yards are located in lenient jails.
explanation.definitionFit: Playpens are small enclosures where infants can move about safely.

clue.text: Son involved in return of desert ruler

indicators.note: involved in places the son's letter inside the turned word
return of says the synonym for desert is read backwards

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side

explanation.surface: A son is caught up in the homecoming of a ruler from the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns RAT into TAR, and 'involved in' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsar was the autocratic emperor of Russia.

clue.text: Avoid offending relation

definitions.meaning: to show consideration for someone's feelings or rules
a reference or connection, as in 'with regard to'

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of upsetting a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour someone is to avoid causing offence, and 'in this regard' means in this relation.

clue.text: Outstanding place is in uproar

indicators.note: something in uproar is in confusion, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A notable spot is suddenly full of commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Special means exceptional, standing out from the ordinary.

clue.text: The first crates used for distribution

indicators.note: used as in worked over or exploited, so the letters gathered are rearranged
first takes the opening letter of the word The

explanation.surface: The best crates are kept for deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes T from 'The'; 'used' rearranges T and CRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatter is a spread or dispersal of things over an area.

clue.text: Moderate monarch follows the heartless parliamentarian

indicators.note: follows puts the monarch's letters after the rest
heartless removes the middle letter of the word the

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A restrained queen comes after an unfeeling Member of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes H out of THE to leave TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate or soften it.

clue.text: Girl almost occupying both sides

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is cut from the word

parts.note: astride means with a leg on either side

explanation.surface: A girl nearly has a foot in each camp.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a female first name, Scandinavian in origin.

clue.text: Eliminating first stops, becomes less severe

indicators.note: eliminating first says the opening letter of the synonym for stops is removed

parts.note: ceases means stops or comes to an end

explanation.surface: Once the first halts are removed, a situation relaxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eliminating first' drops the C from CEASES.
explanation.definitionFit: When pain eases it lessens and grows milder.

clue.text: Ready to tackle main course

parts.note: main is the sea, so this describes a vessel fit to sail across the ocean rather than a diner facing dinner

explanation.definitionFit: A ship fit and safe to put to sea is ready for the ocean, which crossword setters call the main.

clue.text: Rotten chap's cheap food

parts.note: food gone off has turned rotten
Al is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A nasty man's food is low-cost fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal, the organ meat of animals, is inexpensive.

clue.text: Confined without salt; coming back to the point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the confined word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut in or confined

indicators.note: coming back says the salt's name is read backwards

parts.note: nitre is potassium nitrate, a salt

explanation.surface: A prisoner denied salt returns to the main issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so 'Confined' wraps the salt's name after 'coming back' has reversed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent means relevant, bearing directly on the matter in hand.

clue.text: Stuffiness associated with posh eastern music

parts.note: fug is a stuffy, smoky atmosphere in a closed room
U is the label for upper-class usage, so posh

explanation.surface: A stuffy room goes with upper-class oriental tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugue is a contrapuntal composition built on a repeated theme.

clue.text: Gunman?

parts.note: read as gun plus man: a slang word for a pistol that is also a man's first name

explanation.definitionFit: In old American slang a pistol is called a rod, and Rod is also a man's name, so it is both gun and man.

clue.text: Asian trust plans second deployment of wildlife experts

indicators.note: a deployment rearranges forces, so the letters gathered are redistributed
second picks out the second letter of the word plans

explanation.surface: An Asian trust lays out a second stage for its conservation scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' takes L from plans; 'deployment' rearranges ASIAN, TRUST and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturalists study animals and plants in the wild.
